title: Highest temperature in NYC on September 2?
description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent cloud cover, easterly flow, and scattered showers are capping peak temperatures in the mid-70s for New York City on September 2, 2026.** Official and model consensus forecasts from sources such as WeatherBug and WindBorne indicate a high near 73–76 °F under mostly overcast skies, with a 25–40% chance of light rain or drizzle driven by onshore easterly winds of 7–15 mph. These conditions limit daytime heating compared to the climatological average high of ~80.5 °F for the date.

The market’s tight clustering around 74–77 °F (65.5% combined probability) directly tracks this guidance, while lower odds on 78 °F+ or sub-72 °F outcomes reflect the narrow uncertainty band typical 24 hours ahead. Key resolution factors include the official Central Park or LaGuardia maximum, which models show will be suppressed by reduced insolation and marine influence rather than any extreme synoptic shift. Updated NWS or NOAA model runs on September 1–2 remain the primary near-term catalyst that could nudge the distribution within the current mid-70s range.
